newsitem.title: USA: Spectranetics says gets FDA ok for study.
newsitem.headline: Spectranetics says gets FDA ok for study.

text.p: Spectranetics Corp said Monday it has received conditional FDA approval for a clinical study of is Prima laser guidewire.
The company said the device is designed to pass through coronary arteries which are clogged completely by essentially burning holes in them.
The company said the approval was for an Investigational Device Exemption.
The company said the purpose of the study will be to restore blood flow through a totally clogged artery where other devices have failed.
The company said this use may allow treatment to patients who would otherwise be restricted to drug therapy or bypass surgery.
The company said the study calls for patients to be treated with the Prima laser guidewire if they have previously failed treatment with a mechanical guidewire.
The company said the self-controlled study is expected to begin by June and will enroll 120 patients.
The company said a sub-study is included, consisting of a six-month angiographic follow-up for the first 60 patients successfully treated.
The company said results from this study will be combined with results from the Prima studies in Europe and will be submitted to the FDA for pre-market approval.
